brief: Deutsche Bank's macro wrap reports a global bond selloff into Q4, driven by the US-Iran conflict's re-escalation, which pushed Brent crude up 42% from its late-June lows. The 10yr Treasury rose for a 7th straight month in September (+53bps, most since Sep 2022), as resilient growth let the Fed, ECB and BoJ hike again. In the latest session, downward revisions to US core PCE (year-on-year to 3.0% vs 3.3% expected, 3-month annualized rate 2.05%, softest since July 2024) cut priced odds of an October Fed hike from 47% to 37%, though DB's economists expect the next hike in December, not October. That dovish repricing held only at the front end: the 10yr yield still hit a post-2007 high of 5.28% and the 30yr a post-2002 high of 5.63%, while the S&P 500 reversed an early rally to close -0.25%. Trump said Powell should be forced to resign from the Fed Board after an Inspector General report on renovation overruns. Euro Area flash September CPI beat in Germany, France and Italy, pushing DB's CPI tracking to 3.8% and widening the Franco-German spread to 127bps, highest since June 2012, and the Italian-bund spread above 100bps for the first time in a year.
